EXPLANATION: The spectrum lacks any strong carbonyl band near 1650–1750 cm⁻¹, excluding the carboxylic acids and ketones/amides (1,2,3,4,6,9). It also lacks an O–H stretch near 3200–3600 cm⁻¹, disfavoring the alcohol (8). The pattern strongly matches an alkyl sulfonate: two S=O stretches around 1378 and 1210 cm⁻¹ (with an accompanying band at 1153 cm⁻¹), a C–O–S stretch near 1053 cm⁻¹, and strong S–C/S–O–C modes in the 550–650 cm⁻¹ region (535, 582, 615). The CH stretches at 2930/2971 and CH deformation at 1450 are consistent with an aliphatic system (GFQ-003). Candidate 7’s expected CF3/Si–O signatures would typically yield dominant C–F stretches; here the most intense feature is 535 cm⁻¹, better aligned with sulfonate bending. Hence CCCCCS(=O)(=O)OCC (10) fits best.
